summary.text: A 67 year old man with type 2 diabetes complicated by retinopathy and nephropathy, peripheral arterial disease, coronary heart disease, steatosis hepatis and gout presented with a chronic ulcer on his left forefoot existing for about 8 years despite adequate offloading in orthopedic shoes. Fever and elevated inflammation markers at admission led to ciprofloxacin treatment.

Microbiological testing showed a mixed infection and inflammation markers decreased under antibiotics. Negative pressure wound therapy gave only little improvement, so the verrucous wound margin was sampled and showed a highly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. Conventional X-rays showed no signs of bone or joint involvement, and surgical resection was planned after the acute infection abated.

In September 2018 he received deep excision of the carcinoma; histopathology showed an ulcerated, highly differentiated carcinoma 7 mm thick, grade G1, without evidence of lymph node metastases or bone involvement. A second resection in October 2018 was needed because the borders were not reliable in sano, with no further proof of relapse. A split-skin graft covered the wound in November 2018 with good result; the final tumor formula was pT3, cN0, cM0, R0, G1.

summary.text: A woman described as gaunt had a chronic neuropathic ulcer of her right foot for about 8 years and was repeatedly treated by the authors. Her history showed progressed peripheral arterial disease, arterial hypertension, mild pronounced diabetes with an A1c of 5.9% and neuro- and nephropathy stage G3bA2, reactive depression, malnutrition, continuous smoking and several amputations and revascularizations on both feet; she was wheelchair-bound for longer distances.

In May 2018 the ulcer was sampled for the first time because of its suspicious verrucous appearance, and histology showed a highly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the Ackerman carcinoma subtype. A total resection was avoided then because a complicated gangrene on her left foot was being treated; after successful treatment she was discharged to outpatient care with a subsequent resection planned.

In February 2019 she was readmitted with recurring infections and foetid secretion in the area of the cancer. After initial piperacillin/tazobactam she was planned for tumor excision; the primary excision left SCC at the margins, a second resection showed tumor free margins, and a split-skin graft with negative pressure wound therapy covered the wound. Sentinel nodes were inconspicuous, plain films showed no bone involvement, and she refused further incisive surgery; the tumor formula was pT3, cN0, M0, R0, G1.
